A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CRISP study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across appendix and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original WMDP-Bio and WMDP-Cyber experiments on two language models, qualitative generations, hyperparameter trade-offs and SAE feature analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds Harry Potter benchmark comparisons for both language models in Appendix B, Table 2.

M1.justification: The contrastive SAE feature-selection procedure, LoRA optimization and unlearning, retention and coherence losses are unchanged. The Harry Potter evaluation introduces no documented method component or procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v2 adds Harry Potter knowledge unlearning on the multiple-choice benchmark attributed to ELM, evaluated with both models. This substantially broadens coverage beyond the biosecurity and cybersecurity domains evaluated in v1; existing coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The original-model reference and ELM and RMU comparators remain unchanged in the WMDP comparisons. The added Harry Potter evaluation uses the same comparator set.

E3.justification: The added Harry Potter comparison reports unlearning accuracy, MMLU, fluency, concept and overall scores, without the domain-specific retain-accuracy measure reported for WMDP. Existing WMDP settings are unchanged. Harry Potter-specific splits, sample sizes, tuning and overall-score aggregation are not explained.

E4.justification: The qualitative examples, hyperparameter trade-off plots and SAE feature analyses are retained, including the feature-analysis appendix moved from B to C. No new ablation, sensitivity, robustness or error-analysis experiment is introduced.

E5.justification: The WMDP fluency and concept means and standard deviations across 100 prefixes are retained in v1 Table 7 and v2 Table 8. No new run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests are reported; the Harry Potter table supplies point estimates only.

E6.justification: v2 adds a complete two-model Harry Potter comparison, supplying substantive findings outside the original domains. CRISP's unlearning accuracies are 29.52 and 25.65 for Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-2B. Its overall score trails RMU on Llama (53.81 versus 58.02) but leads on Gemma (49.30 versus 41.59). Matched WMDP results and existing qualitative findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The SAE definitions, feature-selection equations, loss formulations, overall-score equation and hyperparameter-selection formulas are mathematically unchanged. Equation punctuation and typesetting edits introduce no new reasoning, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about persistent unlearning, safety-domain performance, knowledge and fluency preservation, and interpretable feature selection.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 and new Appendix B present the Harry Potter evaluation as demonstrating versatility beyond safety domains. Existing mechanism explanations and limitations remain unchanged, including the now-inconsistent statement that evaluation is limited to safety-critical domains.

D1.justification: v1 refers to an unspecified project repository; v2 adds an explicit CRISP code-repository URL in the abstract. Existing implementation, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures are retained. This establishes improved access information, not independently verified repository availability.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work positioning are unchanged. The Harry Potter benchmark is attributed to the already-cited ELM work by Gandikota et al. (2024), without introducing a new cited work or substantive novelty claim.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short Harry Potter appendix subsection and results pointer, updates appendix references, edits the author and affiliation block, adds contact information, and makes limited wording changes. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Harry Potter Table 2 and renumbers the subsequent tables. Appendix tables and prompt boxes reflow, and the title-page author block changes layout. Figures 1–5 retain the same graphics and substantive captions.

improvement.justification: The Harry Potter results provide useful evidence beyond v1's safety-only evaluation, while the explicit repository link improves code discoverability. The gain is limited by sparse documentation of the new experiment and the unrevised safety-only limitation. The mixed Harry Potter ranking, including RMU's higher Llama overall score, also warrants fuller discussion.
